40 photo dump ideas for Instagram

5 min read·Ideas

By Gül Eda Aydemir, indie iOS developer · Updated 28 Oct 2026

Stuck on what to post? Pick the kind of dump you're making and use its eight ideas as a shot list. Most dumps feel right at 8 to 12 slides, so you won't need all of them.

After the ideas: how to order the slides so people swipe all the way to the end.

Weekly photo dump ideas

A weekly dump works because nothing has to happen. Look for small, repeatable moments and one slide that makes people laugh.

  1. The coffee (or tea) of the week — a close-up drink is an easy, friendly opener.
  2. Something you cooked — even toast counts. Hands in the frame make it feel personal.
  3. Your walk or commute — the same street at a different hour reads like a tiny story.
  4. One mirror or outfit shot — one is enough to put you in the dump without a selfie series.
  5. A screenshot that sums up the week — a funny text, a playlist, a weather app. Cover names and numbers.
  6. Something you finished — a book, a workout, a project, a kitchen that is finally clean.
  7. A friend's hands or back — people who aren't posing keep the dump candid.
  8. One blurry, chaotic photo — motion and mess are what make a dump feel real.

Monthly photo dump ideas

Let the month be the theme. Four anchor photos, one per week, keep it in order; the rest fills the gaps.

  1. One photo from each week — four anchors give the month a backbone and an order.
  2. The month's big moment — an event, a trip, a first day, a move.
  3. A seasonal detail — the first strawberries, a wet umbrella, a pumpkin on a doorstep.
  4. A before and after — a haircut, a room, a plant that survived.
  5. Food you'll remember — the dish you'd order again tomorrow.
  6. A ticket, receipt or note — paper details add texture. Blur anything personal.
  7. Something you saw every day — the same mug, the same tree, your cat in a new spot.
  8. A sunset or night shot to close — a calm last slide ends the month softly.

Travel photo dump ideas

Order matters most on a trip. Arrive, look around, eat, slow down, go home.

  1. The arrival — a plane window, a train platform or the first street sign.
  2. A wide establishing shot — a skyline, a bay or a square, so people know where you are.
  3. Local food, up close — street food, a market stall, a long breakfast.
  4. Signs, menus and door numbers — details that say "somewhere else" without a caption.
  5. The best corner of where you stayed — a balcony, a bed with a view, the tiled bathroom.
  6. A candid of your travel partner — or your shadow, if you went alone.
  7. A moment of nothing — waiting for a bus, a bench, feet in the sand.
  8. The way home — a suitcase, a last coffee, the airport floor.

Summer photo dump ideas

Summer dumps run on colour and light. Lean into water, fruit and the long evening sky.

  1. Water in any form — the sea, a pool, a sprinkler, a glass covered in drops.
  2. Sun-faded details — a beach towel, a tan line, a straw hat.
  3. Ice cream before it melts — or after. The melted one is usually funnier.
  4. Long evening light — a sky that is still bright late in the evening says summer on its own.
  5. Fruit — watermelon, cherries, figs: strong colour for a middle slide.
  6. A feet shot — sandals, sand, the end of a pier.
  7. A summer night out — an open-air cinema, string lights, a late dinner outside.
  8. A heat joke — a fan pointed at your face, a weather app showing the temperature.

Year-recap photo dump ideas

The one dump that earns a long carousel. Start with a photo per month, then add the moments people will ask about.

  1. One photo per month — twelve anchors in date order.
  2. The moment everyone asked about — the photo you showed people in person.
  3. Something you tried for the first time — a hobby, a city, a haircut.
  4. A hard month, gently — a quiet photo counts it without oversharing.
  5. The people who were there — a group shot, or a few faces in a row.
  6. Your year in a screenshot — steps, books, a music recap, only if you want to share it.
  7. The photo you almost deleted — imperfect, but it turned out to matter.
  8. A look ahead — a new notebook, an empty calendar, the first sunrise of the year.

How to order the slides in a photo dump

Lead with your strongest photo, change the scale on every swipe and end with something funny. The details:

  1. Start with your strongest photo.Sharp, bright and with one clear subject. It's the slide people see in the feed and on your profile grid.
  2. Mix close-ups and wide shots.A detail, then a place, then a person. When the scale changes on every swipe, the next slide always feels new.
  3. Group colours, or keep time order.Trips read best in date order; a weekly dump looks calmer when similar colours sit side by side.
  4. Put a video or motion shot in the middle.It breaks the rhythm just as attention starts to drop.
  5. End with a funny one.A blooper, a deadpan face or the cat. It rewards everyone who swiped to the end.
  6. Stop at 8 to 12 slides.Instagram allows up to 20, but a tighter dump gets swiped to the end. Save the long version for a year recap.

Want a slot-by-slot template? How to pick photos for a photo dump has a 10-slot order and a checklist. The 20-slide limit comes from Instagram's 2024 carousel update (TechCrunch).

Frequently asked questions

What is a photo dump?

+

A photo dump is an Instagram carousel of loosely connected photos from a week, a month, a trip or an event, posted together with a short caption. It looks casual on purpose, though the best ones are carefully chosen and ordered.

How many photos are in a photo dump?

+

Instagram allows up to 20 photos and videos in one carousel. Most dumps work best with 8 to 12: enough variety to be fun, short enough that people reach the last slide.

What should the first photo of a photo dump be?

+

Your strongest photo: sharp, bright and with one clear subject. The first slide is what people see in the feed and on your grid, so it decides whether anyone swipes.

How often should you post a photo dump?

+

As often as you have enough photos for one. Weekly suits people who take photos most days; monthly is the easiest rhythm to keep up.

Does a photo dump need a theme?

+

A loose one helps. A time span (this week, October), a place or a mood is enough to make the photos feel like they belong together.
